newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong launches new China-linked stock index.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong launches new China-linked stock index.

text.p: HSI Services Ltd, the compiler of Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index, said on Friday it would launch a new China-play stock index in response to a frenzy here for red chip stocks ahead of Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule.

The new index, the Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index, will be launched on Monday and include 32 red chip companies -- Hong Kong-incorporated companies with financial backing from the mainland.

"The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index is designed to meet the increasing demand for a benchmark to gauge the performance of China-affliated companies listed on the stock market," HSI Services chairman Anthony Wong told a news conference.

The index includes Hong Kong's favourite red chips such as Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd, China Resources Enterprise Ltd, COSCO Pacific Ltd, Guangzhou Investment Co Ltd and blue chip Guangdong Investment Ltd.
It also includes smaller red chips such as Poly Investment Holdings Ltd, Hualing Holdings Ltd and Shougang Concord Century Holdings Ltd.
HSI Services said the China-Affiliated Corporations Index is backdated to January 4 1993 with a base value of 1,000 points.
It stood at 2,490.20 at the close of business on Thursday and analysts expected a roaring start.

"It is going to maintain the interest and activity in the red chip stocks but with a stronger institutional bias," said South China Holdings vice chairman Howard Gorges. "Quite a lot of fund managers will want to own stocks in those red chips."
The market capitalisation of the stocks in the index represented 6.4 percent of Hong Kong's total market cap at the end of May compared with 2.7 percent at the end of May 1996.
Turnover in the stocks rose to 15.5 percent of total market turnover from 4.1 percent over the same period.

Analysts said while the index may not supersede the blue chip Hang Seng Index, which represents more than 70 percent of Hong Kong's total market capitalisation, red chips would play an increasingly prominent role as China's influence grows here.
Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule on midnight of June 30.
"These China-affiliated enterprises are going to have greater and greater significance in the Hong Kong stock market," said Abhijit Chakrabortti, senior strategist at Lehman Brothers.
"These companies will eventually play such a prominent role that they will become Hang Seng Index constituents themselves and start to replace some existing constituents."

The companies in the index are incorporated in Hong Kong and at least 35 percent of their shareholding is held directly or indirectly by Chinese state-owned organisations or provincial or municipal authorities in China, HSI Services said.
Thirty-nine red chip companies in Hong Kong fell within that category, it said.
Stocks included in Hong Kong's Hang Seng China Enterprises Index, or H-share index, are not included. H-shares are stocks of China-incorporated companies listed in Hong Kong.
Constituent stocks have been listed for at least 12 months on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong and have a trading record of at least 12 months under the control of a Chinese entity.
Each stock is weighted so that it will influence the index in proportion to its market value and weightings will be updated on a monthly basis, HSI Services said.
Like the Hang Seng Index, the Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index, will be reviewed on a quarterly basis to see if any changes in its constituents should be made.
